newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down after midsession reversal.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down after midsession reversal.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower after early gains on the back of a lower-than-expected hike in LME stocks fizzled by midsession as London spreads weakened.

There was still support at current price levels as long as the backwardation or cash premium over three months on LME stayed firm, though a market that made a fresh recent high and closed lower was disconcerting, Lawson Spence of Smith Barney said.
The LME backwardation eased about $20 Tuesday to $165/$170.
"Stocks are at low levels and generally everything looks on track for good demand," Spence said, but added that Tuesday's weak close was a "caution flag".
LME stocks rose just 200 tonnes Tuesday to 131,475 tonnes.
A broker said that when the market was on the highs and metal was being offered, there was a feeling that everyone was long and this took the steam out of the market.
March COMEX settled 0.90 cent weaker at 105.45 cents per pound, traded 107.60 to 104.90 cents. Spot January went out 1.10 cents down at 108.20 cents.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots compared to Monday's official 6,652 lots.
